verdict.rationale: Crossmint documents a user-approved mandate before an agent can spend. For wallets, the agent's signer key is bound to a permission set the user signs off on (spend cap, counterparties, time window), enforced onchain and revocable. For cards, the user authorizes an order intent with a fixed allowance and expiration, verified with a card-network passkey ceremony. Missing for 10: no documented per-purchase or step-up confirmation for sensitive spends once a mandate exists (wallet delegation explicitly runs with 'no user prompt per action'), and no independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, sensitive agent spending requires my documented approval — a confirmation step, signed mandate, or per-purchase consent — before money moves
